title: Kid Thomas's simple style and playing behind it
summary: Ralph asks about Kid Thomas's sparse trumpet style; Hall says simple lead makes it easy to fill in.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Can I ask one of the questions that I just thought of? This is the last one. This goes back quite a ways. I guess I wouldn't hardly get born yet, but I wondered, I've heard Thomas play and his style seems to, yeah, kid Thomas play and his style seems to not to go too high and not to hit too many notes. And I wondered if that would be a good style for a firenip to play with. What you mean Thomas Valentine? Yeah, Thomas. What, the trumpet player? No, if it's easier for him to play firenip with him, you mean. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I wondered how that trumpet style would be to play with, to play firenip with him.
Yeah, I imagine it's all right. I started with Thomas because Thomas is still playing the same way. Yeah, I know you played. Yeah.
That's why I asked the question. Well, my mom said once, so it's easier to play a simple lead than

somebody that's too fancy. Yeah. Oh yeah. When you usually, if you get a trumpet player, he's trying to play like a clown and making all these notes, then you clash with each other. That's why I thought of Thomas because he plays very few notes. Very few notes and very simple. You can understand what he's playing. A lot of trumpet players be playing something you don't understand what they're playing. You see? The clown is just mostly the fill in anymore. That's a good, nice idea, sure.

Well, I guess that's all I have to add. That just came to my mind then because I knew you didn't play with Thomas. Oh yeah, sure. Thomas, I guess, still plays the same style you always play. Yeah, I always do.
